note: Instrumented run killed at ~540s by shell watchdog during thrash; 7 gauges captured before kill. Gauges mirrored to stderr and reconstructed here verbatim.
finding: FIRST ANOMALOUS BOUNDARY = SEG1_AFTER_READ: the segment materialization loop accumulates ALL of segment 1's tensors (13824 MiB) in the arrays dictionary BEFORE any update; combined with the already-resident core+segment 0 (2902 MiB), the footprint hits 30616 MiB (30.6 GiB, at the 32 GiB physical edge) and the system enters swap thrash during segment 1's update. The defect is the BATCH-THEN-UPDATE materialization shape: per-tensor reads accumulate in a dictionary instead of being updated into the model one tensor at a time (read→update→drop per tensor keeps peak at core+prev+ONE tensor). No release boundary exists in this code path at all (release never runs before the whole-graph forward).
